questions.q: An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic transformation starting from the point $A$ and coming back to the same point by tracing the path $A \to B \to C \to A$ as shown in the diagram. The total work done in the process is _____J.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Work done is given by area enclosed in the $PvsV$ cyclic graph or $VvsP$ cyclic graph

Sign of work is positive for clockwise cyclic process for $VvsP$ graph.

Work done in cyclic process = area inside the figure

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times ( 30 - 10 ) \times ( 30 - 10 ) = 200kPa - {dm}^{3}$

$= 200 \times 1000Pa - L = 2L - bar = 200J$

questions.q:
The number of endothermic process/es from the following is _______.

A. ${I}_{2} ( g ) \to 2I ( g )$

B.~$HCl ( g ) \to H ( g ) + Cl ( g )$

C. ${H}_{2}O ( l ) \to {H}_{2}O ( g )$

D. $C ( s ) + {O}_{2} ( g ) \to {CO}_{2} ( g )$

E. Dissolution of ammonium chloride in water
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The decomposition reactions are endothermic reactions. The reactions& ${I}_{2} ( g ) \to 2I ( g )$~and~$HCl ( g ) \to H ( g ) + Cl ( g )$~are decomposition reactions. The heat vaporisation is an endothermic reaction. Hence, the conversion of~${H}_{2}O \left(l\right)\overset{}{→}{H}_{2}O\left(g\right)$~is endothermic process. The heat of combustion is an exothermic process. The heat involved in~$C ( s ) + {O}_{2} ( g ) ⟶ {CO}_{2} ( g )$~is heat of combustion.~The dissolution of ammonium chloride in water is an endothermic process. ${NH}_{4}Cl ( s ) \to {NH}_{4}^{+} ( aq ) + {Cl}^{−} ( aq ) ; \Delta H = + 15 . 1kJ / mol .

$

questions.q:
The standard entropy change for the reaction

$4Fe \left(s\right) + 3{O}_{2} \left($g\right) \to $2{Fe}_{2}{O}_{3}\left($s\right)$~is~$- 550JK^{- 1}$~at~$298K$

[Given : The standard enthalpy change for the reaction is $- 165kJ{mol}^{- 1}$]. The temperature in $K$ at which the reaction attains equilibrium is (Nearest Integer)

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$4Fe\left(s\right) + 3{O}_{2}\left(g\right) \to 3{Fe}_{2}{O}_{3}\left(s\right){ΔS}_{r} = - 550J / K$

${ΔS}_{r} = - 165kJ / mole$

At equilibrium~$\Delta G = 0$

$T = \left(\dfrac{ΔH}{ΔS}\right)~at equilibrium

=\dfrac{- 165 \times {10}^{3}}{- 550} =$300K$

$

questions.q:
One mole of an ideal gas at& $350K$ is in a $2 . 0L$ vessel of thermally conducting walls, which are in contact with the surroundings. It undergoes isothermal reversible expansion from~$2 . 0L$~to~$3 . 0L$ against a constant pressure of~$4atm$. The change in entropy of the surroundings $( ∆ S )$ is _____ $JK^{– 1}$ (Nearest integer)

Given:~$R = 8 . 314JK^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The first law of thermodynamics for isothermal process& $Q = - W$

The~$W$~for isothermal reversible process is

$W = - nRTln\dfrac{V2}{V1}$

$∆ S = \dfrac{Q}{T}$

$∆ {S}_{surrounding} = - nRln\dfrac{V2}{V1}$

$= - 1 \times 8 . 314 \times 2 . 303 \times log\dfrac{3}{2}$

$= - 3 . 37{JK}^{- 1}$

$≃ - 3{JK}^{- 1}$

The given process is mentioned as isothermal reversible process hence the~$∆ {S}_{surrounding}$& is calculated.

questions.q:
At $25 ° C, 50g$ of iron reacts with $HCl$ to form ${FeCl}_{2}$. The evolved hydrogen gas expands against a constant pressure of $1bar$. The work done by the gas during this expansion is -_______ $J$.

(Round off to the Nearest Integer)

[Given : $R = 8 . 314J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}$. Assume, hydrogen is an ideal gas]

[Atomic mass off Fe is $55 . 85u$]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$T = 298K, R = 8 . 314\dfrac{J}{molK}$

→ Chemical reaction is

$\mathop{Fe}_{50g} + 2HCl \to \mathop{FeCl2}_{P = 1bar} + {H}_{2} \left(g\right)$

=\dfrac{50}{55 . 85}$mol$

→ Work done for $1mol$ gas

$= - {P}_{ext} \times \Delta V$

$= {Δn}_{g}RT$

$= - 1 \times8 . 314 \times298J$

→ Work done for \dfrac{50}{55 . 85}mol of gas

$= - 8 . 314 \times298 \times $\dfrac{50}{55 . 85}$J$

$= - 2218 . 059J$

$≃ - 2218J

$

questions.q: $1$ mole of ideal gas is allowed to expand reversibly and adiabatically from a temperature of $27 ° C$. The work done is $3kJ{mol}^{- 1}$. The final temperature of the gas is _____~$K$ (Nearest integer). Given ${C}_{v} = 20J{mol}^{- 1}K^{- 1}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
From first law of thermodynamics:
$∆ U = q + W$
We know for adiabatic process,
$∴ q = 0$

$∴ \Delta U = w ⇒ m \times {C}_{v} \times ∆ T = w$

$⇒ 1 \times 20 \times \left[{T}_{2} - 300\right] = - 3000$

$⇒ {T}_{2} - 300 = - 150$

$∴ {T}_{2} = 150K$

questions.q:
For independent process at $300K$.

Process $\Delta H / {kJmol}^{- 1}$ $\Delta S / {JK}^{- 1}$
$A$ $- 25$ $- 80$
$B$ $- 22$ $40$
$C$ $25$ $- 50$
$D$ $22$ $20$

The number of non-spontaneous process from the following is _____ .
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The relation& between change in Gibbs free energy, change in enthalpy and change in entropy can be written as follows,

$\Delta G = \Delta H - T \Delta S$

If~$∆ G$~is $+ ve$ , then the process is said to be non-spontaneous and if $∆ G$~is~$- ve$~then the process is said to be spontaneous.

$A: \Delta G\left({Jmol}^{- 1}\right) = - 25 \times {10}^{3} + 80 \times 300: - ve$

$B: \Delta G\left({Jmol}^{- 1}\right) = - 22 \times {10}^{3} - 40 \times 300: - ve$

$C: \Delta G\left({Jmol}^{- 1}\right) = 25 \times {10}^{3} + 300 \times 50; + ve$

$D: \Delta G\left({Jmol}^{- 1}\right) = 22 \times {10}^{3} - 20 \times 300: + ve$

Processes $C$ and $D$ are non-spontaneous.

questions.q:
The molar heat capacity for an ideal gas at constant pressure is $20 . 785JK^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$. The change in internal energy is $5000J$ upon heating it from $300K$ to $500K$. The number of moles of the gas at constant volume is____

(Given: $R = 8 . 314JK^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Molar specific heat capacity at constant pressure is defined as the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of one mole of a substance through $1K$ or $1 ° C$ at constant pressure. It is denoted by~${C}_{p, m}$.

Molar specific heat capacity at constant volume~is defined as the amount of heat energy required to raise the temperature of one mole of a substance through $1K$ or $1 ° C$ at constant volume. It is denoted by~${C}_{v, m}$.

${C}_{v, m} = \dfrac{1}{n}\dfrac{∆ U}{∆ T}$

${C}_{p, m} = {C}_{v, m} + R$

$⇒ {C}_{v, m} = 20 . 785 - 8 . 314 = 12 . 471{Jk}^{- 1}{ml}^{- 1}$

$\Delta U = {nC}_{v, m}\Delta T$

$⇒ n = \dfrac{5000}{12 . 471 \times 200} = \dfrac{25}{12 . 471} \approx 2$

questions.q: The enthalpy of combustion of propane, graphite and dihydrogen at $298K$ are: $- 2220 . 0kJ{mol}^{- 1}$, $- 393 . 5kJ{mol}^{- 1}$ and $- 285 . 8kJ{mol}^{- 1}$ respectively. The magnitude enthalpy of formation of propane  \left({C}_{3}{H}_{8}\right)$ is _____ ${kJmol}^{- 1}$. (Nearest integer)$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction can be written as follows,

${C}_{3}{H}_{8\left(g\right)} + 5{O}_{2}\overset{}{→}3{CO}_{2} + 4{H}_{2}O; ∆ H = - 2220 . 0kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

${C}_{graphite} + {O}_{2\left(g\right)}\overset{}{→}{CO}_{2}\left(g\right); ∆ H = - 393 . 5kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

${H}_{2}\left(g\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}{O}_{2\left(g\right)}\overset{}{→}{H}_{2}O\left(l\right); ∆ H = - 285 . 8kJ{mol}^{- 1}$

Now, the formation reaction of propane is

$3C\left(graphite\right) + 4{H}_{2\left(g\right)} \to {C}_{3}{H}_{8\left(g\right)} ∆ {H}_{f} = 3 ∆ {H}_C^{°}\left(graphite\right) + 4 ∆ {H}_C^{°}\left({H}_{2\left(g\right)}\right) - ∆ {H}_C^{°}\left(propane\right) ∆ {H}_{f} = 3 \times \left(- 393 . 5\right) + 4 \times \left(- 285 . 8\right) - \left(- 2220\right) = - 103 . 7kJ{mol}^{- 1}$
